title: Exclusive | FTX’s Old Bitcoin-Mining Assets Are Now Part of the AI Boom
source_used: Blockhead, The Crypto Times and The Tokenist (all 12 Oct 2026), relaying The Wall Street Journal exclusive and SWI Group's announcement; the WSJ page returned HTTP 401
key_facts: SWI Group, a Singapore-incorporated, Amsterdam-listed digital infrastructure company (ticker SWICH), announced on Monday 12 Oct 2026 a capital increase of 800 million euros (about $900 million) from unnamed institutional investors, valuing it at 6.1 billion euros and taking the equity it has raised since March past 1 billion euros.
The money is for power infrastructure, compute deployments and its development pipeline in Europe and the US.

SWI took control of Genesis Digital Assets, a former bitcoin miner into which Alameda Research, Sam Bankman-Fried's trading firm, put about $1.15 billion from 2021; SWI closed a $500 million purchase of about 38.3 percent on 15 Jun 2026, held more than 70 percent by 25 Aug 2026, and says Genesis Digital holds more than 1.3 gigawatts of grid connections across 15 facilities.

SWI's founder and chief executive Max-Hervé George told the Wall Street Journal that SWI plans to market the Genesis sites in Texas, North Carolina, South Carolina and Sweden to hyperscale cloud providers (the largest cloud-computing companies), has 'zero interest' in mining bitcoin and is selling the last three small mining sites in Kazakhstan.

The FTX Recovery Trust dropped, with prejudice, its roughly $1.15 billion clawback suit against Genesis Digital on 15 Jun 2026, the day SWI closed its stake; the dismissal notice mentions no settlement or payment and neither side has disclosed what, if anything, the estate received; George told the WSJ all legal disputes have been settled.
Per Blockhead, the WSJ reports the estate had called the investment 'one of Bankman-Fried's most reckless' and the Kazakh assets 'virtually worthless'.
The Tokenist notes that grid access is a key asset but not proof of operational AI capacity or revenue.
quote_evidence: SWI Group, the Singapore-incorporated, Amsterdam-listed digital infrastructure company that took control of former Bitcoin miner Genesis Digital Assets this year, has raised €800 million (about $900 million) to expand its data centre and AI compute capacity, the company announced on Monday.
Max-Hervé George, SWI's founder and chief executive, told the Wall Street Journal the company has “zero interest” in bitcoin mining.
Neither the trust nor SWI has disclosed what, if anything, the estate received in return.
why_it_matters_hint: Power connections built for crypto mining are being repurposed for AI computing, and a failed exchange's old holding ends up in the AI build-out.
event_date: SWI's raise was announced on 12 Oct 2026; the WSJ exclusive is dated 12 Oct 2026 04:01 UTC; the stake purchase and lawsuit dismissal were on 15 Jun 2026.
notes: The WSJ page returned HTTP 401 (paywall) and was not opened. The text was read in three relays of the same news: Blockhead (read in full), The Crypto Times and The Tokenist, which all credit SWI's announcement and the WSJ interview. Details attributed to the WSJ come from those relays only. CONFIRMED rests on the company's own announcement as reported by three outlets; the investors are unnamed and the claims about plans are the chief executive's. The 15 Jun 2026 purchase was reported then by Data Center Dynamics and Tech Times (headlines seen), so the takeover itself is older; the new items are the raise and the WSJ exclusive.
